newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher but below 2,000 on CAC.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher but below 2,000 on CAC.

text.p: French shares finished firmer but failed to breach 2,000 on the CAC-40 index, as market operators grew cautious ahead of U.S. jobless figures due on Friday.
The market got a lift from companies' first-half profits, which were well received, and strong German second-quarter growth statistics, which should feed through to the French economy, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 11.46 points or 0.58 percent at 1,996.23, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,003 from 1992 on Wednesday's close.
Volume was a respectable 3.59 billion francs.
* Christian Noyer, senior aide to Economy Minister Jean Arthuis, reaffirmed that France would meet its Maastricht treaty target of three percent of GDP by 1997

* He added that France and Germany both had growth of 0.7 percent over the first half and that the question was whether France would see growth of between 1.5-two percent, or stronger growth of 2.5 or three percent
* But the mood in equities was cautious and operators would watch tomorrow's U.S. jobless data for clues on the next move on U.S. interest rates.
* Danone rises 29 francs to 721 on broker upgrades
* Goldman Sachs upgraded Danone to "trading buy" from "market performer," while Societe Generale Delahaye upped it to "outperform" from "neutral"

* Several stocks traded on expectations of a shakeup of the constituents of the CAC-40 index. Among risers who might join the index were Usinor-Sacilor, up 3.05 at 75.95, Sodexho 60 to 2,458, AGF 2.90 at 134.60, Cetelem four to 1,051.
* Stocks which could leave the index were Cie Bancaire down two francs to 503, Thomson-CSF down 0.5 to 146.30, and Saint-Louis two to 1,178.
* Eurotunnel, unchanged at 7.90 francs, was also among those rumoured to be leaving CAC index.
* Club Med rose 6.50 francs to 378.50, helped by chairman's reiteration of 1997 profit target of 400 million francs

* Elf Aquitaine down 3.10 to 379.40. Societe Generale Delahaye analyst Aymeric de Villaret upgraded the oil major to "outperform" from "neutral," citing the delay in allowing Iraqi oil sales in the world market and the climb in crude oil prices
* Lagardere, up 3.90 francs at 121.90 benefits from a newspaper report which said the French parliamentary defence committee favours its bid in the Thomson SA privatisation
* Cerus busy, up 11.30 francs at 109.80 on expectations of a sale of its stake in Valeo.
* Valeo was up 4.50 francs at 262.50. It announced first-half profit of 656 million francs and maintained a sales forecast for the year of 28.5 billion francs
